author: Justin Begley Appalachian Newspapers
title: Local Girl Scout rallies to reach camp goal following diabetes diagnosis | News | paintsvilleherald.com
text:
An eight-year-old Girl Scout is pressing forward with her cookie sales goal after a recent Type 1 diabetes diagnosis, determined not to let the autoimmune disease stand in the way of attending camp this summer.
Breanna Vanhoose, troop leader for Girl Scout Troop 1947, is supporting her daughter, Aubrey Vanhoose, a first-grade student at Paintsville Elementary School, as she works to sell enough cookies to earn her way to camp.
“My daughter was recently diagnosed with Type 1 Diabetes,” said Vanhoose. “There’s not too many people around here who have that, especially children. Where it happened during the middle of cookie season, we have all of these cookies with a goal. Each year, there is a goal to sell enough Girl Scout cookies to get to Girl Scout camp. They learn so many things and get so many experiences at camp.”
The diagnosis came in the midst of cookie season, leaving the troop, which consists of 22 girls in total, with inventory to sell and a goal still to reach. Vanhoose acknowledged the irony of the situation but said her daughter remains determined.
“Now we’re kind of stuck with the cookies,” she said. “We’ve acknowledged the irony of it, that a Type 1 Diabetic is selling cookies and she’s only eight years old. Even though it’s hard on her adjusting to it, the needle pokes and stuff, she has stayed strong. It’s difficult for her because people are asking her how they taste or they offer to buy them for her and that makes things a little difficult. We’re still trying to wrap our minds around it and get used to it. I don’t want this new diagnosis to affect her being a child. I want her to be able to do anything else a child can do.”
Vanhoose said the family hopes sharing Aubrey’s story will inspire others facing challenges of their own.
“We’re just trying to let people know that this little girl still has goals,” Vanhoose said. “This autoimmune disease is not getting in her way or stopping her from achieving her goals. I hope this can show other people that no matter what they’re facing in life, they don’t have to give up.”
As Aubrey continues adjusting to daily insulin checks and lifestyle changes, her mother said the focus remains on encouragement and support.
“I’m just trying as a mom to help her see that we’re supporting her,” she said. “She is truly a warrior going through what she’s facing right now.”
For those who would like to help support Aubrey you can do so by visiting, www.digitalcookie.girlscouts.org/scout/aubrey276541.
